subject: Next steps — ZelosHealth discovery: embeddings, rerank + streaming funcalls
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@zeloshealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@zeloshealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps — ZelosHealth discovery: embeddings, rerank + streaming funcalls

Hi Liam / Priya —

Thanks again for a productive call earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive: 

Key pain points you reiterated
- Triage latency: current system struggles to return ranked recommendations under load, which impacts clinician workflow.
- Cost vs quality: need to reduce per-query cost for daily triage volume while preserving recall for critical cases.
- Structured extraction: downstream EHR ingestion needs normalized fields (diagnosis codes, urgency flags).

What we heard as goals
- End-to-end triage throughput ~200 reqs/min with P95 latency < 300ms for the user-facing path.
- Robust reranking step to surface high-precision candidates for clinician review.
- Deterministic structured outputs (JSON schema) for EHR mapping and auditability.

Proposed product fit / approach from Redwood
- Hybrid pipeline: lightweight embeddings for recall + neural reranker for precision. Embeddings used for approximate nearest neighbor prefilter; reranker runs on top-k.
- Streaming responses + function-calls for stepwise extraction: stream intermediate tokens for UI responsiveness; use function-calls to emit structured EHR fields and signal when to persist to the chart.
- SDK changes: small helper for streaming+funcall orchestration, and a recommended client-side cache for patient prefix context to reduce tokens.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Share a short architecture sketch and sample SDK call (attached). Action: Redwood (Jasmine) — attached 'sdk-integration-sketch.png'.
2) Technical deep-dive with eng + security: 60–75m to cover throughput targets, quantization/model variants, SLOs, and data residency. Proposed windows: Wed Oct 21 or Thu Oct 22 morning (PST). Action: Zelos to confirm availability.
3) You to share a small sample of de-identified triage snippets (500–1,000 docs) and top-priority fields for structured extraction. Action: Zelos.
4) We will prep a cost/latency projection for two options: (A) embeddings + rerank on medium-sized model with streaming; (B) reranker-heavy architecture using a larger quantized reranker model. Action: Redwood (Ben + Neha).

Attachments: Zelos_DRP_v1.pdf (6 pages, high-level data retention & flow), sdk-integration-sketch.png (client/server sequence).

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the tech deep-dive and loop in our infra lead. Thanks again — feels like a good fit.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jasmine.liu@redwood.com]

Thanks Jasmine — this is very clear and matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Priority SLA: P95 < 300ms for the clinician UI path is our target. Anything above that materially harms adoption.
- Daily throughput: roughly 200 reqs/min during peak hours; our batch/async pipeline runs separately.
- Security/Data residency: we need SOC 2 evidence and to confirm data-in-transit encryption + EU residency options for later phases.
- Pricing: can you provide a ballpark for both option A and B you mentioned (per 1k queries / per 1M tokens)? We need that for our procurement check.

We can share a de-identified sample export by EOD Tue Oct 20. For the deep-dive, Wed Oct 21 9–11am PST works for us (prefer earlier).

Also looping Priya who will own procurement/security questions.

Cheers,

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — ZelosHealth discovery: embeddings, rerank + streaming funcalls

Quick technical follow-up with a pragmatic path to hit the P95 < 300ms target: 

- Prefilter + rerank: Use a 128-dim dense embedding for ANN prefilter (faiss / pinecone equivalent) returning top-50, then run a compact reranker (quantized 8-bit) on top-50. This keeps reranker compute bounded and improves P95.
- Streaming + funcalls: stream tokens for the UI (first token latencies) while concurrently invoking a function-call at the end of streaming to return normalized JSON fields. This lets the UI render progressive hints while keeping a deterministic record for the EHR.
- Caching/batching: enable per-patient prefix cache and micro-batching (10–20 reqs) at the service edge to improve GPU utilization.

I attached a minimal sample repo with the SDK patterns we propose (link below). That repo includes an example streaming function-call that emits a 'diagnosis' object and an 'urgency' enum.

Sample links / artifacts:
- SDK sample repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/zelos-embed-rerank
- Recommended model variants: rwin-3b-quant (reranker), ephraim-1.4b (embeddings superset)

Ben / Jasmine: I can produce a short cost projection for options A/B once Liam shares the de-identified sample. Also happy to prepare a one-page SOC2 evidence checklist for Priya.

Attachment: sdk-integration-sketch.png (client/server flow).

—Neha
